lesson.title: Have, There Is, Need and Want

cardFrench.note: English 'the fruit' and Spanish la fruta are mass nouns. French normally uses the plural les fruits for fruit in general; un fruit is one piece. The Reader's des fruits frais uses the same plural.
As Spanish té (tea) differs from te (you), French thé (tea) differs from the pronoun te (you): thé has an h and an accent.

cardFrench.en: Do you have fresh orange juice?
cardFrench.french: Vous avez du jus d'orange pressé ?
cardFrench.note: Pressé renders the source's natural: freshly squeezed, not from a carton. Vous covers the source's tienen (ustedes: you all / the café) as well as polite singular you. Avoir expresses possession here, as tener does in Spanish.

cardFrench.french: Il y a du pain grillé ?
cardFrench.note: Il y a stays the same for singular and plural (there is / there are), like Spanish hay.

cardFrench.french: J'ai besoin d'une serviette, s'il vous plaît.
cardFrench.note: Avoir besoin de + noun does the work of Spanish necesitar. De becomes d' before a vowel: d'une.

cardFrench.en: I'd like a tea without sugar.
cardFrench.french: Je voudrais un thé sans sucre.
cardFrench.note: Je voudrais translates the English face 'I'd like'. It is not the form-for-form match of the Spanish line: quiero is literally je veux (I want). Je voudrais corresponds to quisiera, which the source note gives as the softer, more polite alternative. Je veux sounds blunt to a server in French, so je voudrais is the usual way to order.

cardFrench.en: Do you have to pay at the register?
cardFrench.french: Il faut payer à la caisse ?
cardFrench.note: Il faut + infinitive is impersonal (one must / you have to), like Spanish hay que + infinitive.
French says avoir faim, as Spanish says tener hambre ('I have hunger'). Très goes before faim.

readerFrench.es: En un café de Oaxaca, Emma le dice al mesero Luis: Tengo mucha hambre.
readerFrench.en: In a café in Oaxaca, Emma tells the server Luis: I'm very hungry.
readerFrench.french: Dans un café à Oaxaca, Emma dit au serveur Luis : J'ai très faim.

readerFrench.en: Emma: Do you have fresh orange juice?
readerFrench.french: Emma : Vous avez du jus d'orange pressé ?

readerFrench.es: Luis: Sí, y también hay fruta fresca con el desayuno.
readerFrench.en: Luis: Yes, and there is also fresh fruit with breakfast.
readerFrench.french: Luis : Oui, et il y a aussi des fruits frais avec le petit-déjeuner.
Emma : Il y a du pain grillé ?

readerFrench.es: Luis: Sí, el pan tostado viene con mantequilla y mermelada.
readerFrench.en: Luis: Yes, the toast comes with butter and jam.
readerFrench.french: Luis : Oui, le pain grillé est servi avec du beurre et de la confiture.

readerFrench.es: Emma: Quiero un té sin azúcar y una cuchara, por favor.
readerFrench.en: Emma: I'd like a tea without sugar and a spoon, please.
readerFrench.french: Emma : Je voudrais un thé sans sucre et une cuillère, s'il vous plaît.

readerFrench.es: Emma: También necesito un tenedor y una servilleta, por favor.
readerFrench.en: Emma: I also need a fork and a napkin, please.
readerFrench.french: Emma : J'ai aussi besoin d'une fourchette et d'une serviette, s'il vous plaît.

readerFrench.es: Luis: Claro, y hay que pagar en la caja al final.
readerFrench.en: Luis: Sure, and you have to pay at the register at the end.
readerFrench.french: Luis : Bien sûr, et il faut payer à la caisse à la fin.

forms.explanation: Je voudrais matches the English 'I'd like'. The Spanish line uses quiero, which is literally je veux. Je voudrais corresponds to quisiera, the softer form in the source note. French prefers the softer form when ordering.

readerPair.en: Emma: I also need a fork and a napkin, please.
readerPair.french: Emma : J'ai aussi besoin d'une fourchette et d'une serviette, s'il vous plaît.

forms.englishPrompt: Put this Reader line into French: 'Emma: I also need a fork and a napkin, please.' Hint: use the French expression that does the work of Spanish necesitar.

forms.explanation: Avoir besoin de + noun does the work of necesitar. De becomes d' before a vowel and is repeated before each noun. Aussi follows the conjugated verb.

modesMatchingPolicy.spaceBeforePunctuation: A regular space, a no-break space, a narrow no-break space or no space before ? and : are all accepted.
modesMatchingPolicy.apostrophes: Straight and curly apostrophes are equivalent.
modesMatchingPolicy.speakerLabel: The speaker label ('Emma :' or 'Luis :') is optional in learner input and is stripped before comparison.
modesMatchingPolicy.caseAndFinalPunctuation: Initial capital and final punctuation are not scored.
modesMatchingPolicy.accents: Accents are part of the expected spelling. A response that differs only in accents is reported as a near miss showing the correct accents, not as a silent pass or a plain fail.

sourceNotes: Setting and title follow the source: Desayuno en Oaxaca, with Emma and the server Luis. Draft French title: Petit-déjeuner à Oaxaca, held in readerTitle.
All 15 English card faces and kinds are copied from SOURCE.words in source order (9 terms, then 6 phrases). Each card carries its Spanish face and source index.
All 8 Reader English lines are copied from READER.native. Each line carries its Spanish target line and index.
Card and Reader indices are 0-based. Mode, form and speaking answers are held as refs or hidden metadata, never in prompt text.
Focus mapping: tener (possession and tener hambre) to avoir; hay to il y a; necesitar to avoir besoin de; hay que + infinitive to il faut + infinitive.

Querer contrast: the Spanish source uses quiero on card 12 and Reader line 5, while the English faces say 'I'd like'. The French follows the English with je voudrais. Quiero is literally je veux. Je voudrais corresponds to quisiera, which the source note names as the softer form. The English faces are unchanged.
Source 'natural' (freshly squeezed, not from a carton) is rendered pressé on card 9 and Reader line 1.
Source la fruta / 'the fruit' (mass) is rendered les fruits on card 4, consistent with des fruits frais in Reader line 2.

Reader line 2 uses avec le petit-déjeuner for source con el desayuno / 'with breakfast'. Reader line 4 uses est servi avec for source viene con / 'comes with'; this is a wording shift for idiom, not a literal match.

Notes marked noteBasis 'source-note' adapt a note in SOURCE.words. 'source-focus' notes explain the lesson focus. 'adjudication' notes are added by this pass. Cards with note null have no source note.
Hear mode is partner-read from the page only. No recorded audio or speech recognition exists or is proposed for any mode, form or speaking objective.
This adjudication is an AI pass made without tools or repository access. Parity was checked only against the SOURCE and READER text pasted into the request. It is not a qualified review.

acceptedChanges.change: Removed 'Expected answer: la serviette.' from the recall prompt. The answer is now only answerRef cardFrench[6].french.

Took option (a) as instructed. Je voudrais stays on card 12, Reader line 5 and its form. The card note, form explanation and sourceNotes now say that the Spanish uses quiero (literally je veux) and that je voudrais matches the English 'I'd like' and the source note's quisiera. The 'querer/quisiera to je voudrais' equivalence line was removed.
Removed 'as … does in Reader index N' from every form prompt. readerIndex, readerPair and answerRef are metadata. formsAnswerPolicy requires the French Reader to be hidden during forms.
Replaced 'Using il y a / avoir besoin de / il faut / je voudrais / avoir' hints with hints that name the Spanish source structure or the function, without giving French words.
Fixed the Reader line 0 context: Emma speaks to the server Luis. The prompt now uses the exact English Reader line.
Added a form on Reader line 1 (tienen to vous avez), so tener for possession is covered apart from the hunger idiom. There are now six forms.
Speaking objective 1 now reads 'Ask if they have fresh orange juice (freshly squeezed)', restoring the tener framing.

Removed French from the speaking prompts and restored the source wording ('hungry', no 'also'). Model answers are hidden metadata. Both the plain and très / aussi / s'il vous plaît variants are accepted.
Card 4 French changed from le fruit to les fruits, with a note explaining the mass sense and the link to the Reader's des fruits frais. The English face 'the fruit' is unchanged.
Replaced 'never changes form' with 'stays the same for singular and plural, like Spanish hay' on card 10 and in the form explanation.
Added readerTitle with es 'Desayuno en Oaxaca' and draft French 'Petit-déjeuner à Oaxaca', marked unreviewed. readerFrench stays an array, so reader indices are unchanged.
Added es, index and sourceRef to every card and Reader line, and sourceRef with en and es to every mode, form and speaking objective. sourceParityVerified stays false.

Dropped the pressé sentence from card 0 and the filler notes on cards 1, 2, 3, 6, 7 and 8 (now null). Card 5 now carries the thé/te contrast that mirrors the source's té/te note. Every remaining note has a noteBasis.
Card 9 note now says vous covers the source's tienen (ustedes: you all / the café) as well as polite singular you.
Reader line 2 changed from au petit-déjeuner to avec le petit-déjeuner, matching 'with breakfast' / con el desayuno.

Added modesMatchingPolicy: optional space before ? and :, apostrophe equivalence, optional speaker label, unscored case and final punctuation, and an accent near-miss rule. It applies to type, write and forms.

Every mode has audioRef null, an explicit partnerOnly flag and its own gates, all false. Hear is partnerOnly true. Say has asrRef null and self-check or partner-check only. Forms and speaking objectives carry the same false gates.
Removed the private-draft claims (Lyon title, Québec rôties, pronunciation tips) from sourceNotes. They appear only as an unverifiable residual.

The see-mode prompt no longer embeds the French string and uses stimulusRef instead. Form answers are the exact full Reader French lines with the full es/en/french pair attached. Added qualifiedHumanReview false and aiAdjudicationCountsAsReview false to the gates.

residuals: Every French string is an unreviewed AI draft. No native or qualified French reviewer has checked any of it, and this adjudication is not a qualified review. All top-level and per-item gates stay false.
No tools or repository files were used. Parity was checked only against the pasted SOURCE and READER, so a human diff against the repository source is still needed.
Pressé for 'natural' / 'fresh' needs confirmation. Alternatives a reviewer may prefer are du jus d'orange frais or une orange pressée.
Card 4 les fruits pairs a French plural with the English face 'the fruit'. A reviewer or the owner should confirm this over le fruit.
Spelling of petit-déjeuner: the hyphenated noun is accepted by some references, while others prefer petit déjeuner. This affects readerTitle and Reader line 2.
Reader line 4 est servi avec is not a literal match for viene con / 'comes with'. A reviewer should confirm it over vient avec.
Reader line 0 uses à Oaxaca for de Oaxaca / 'in Oaxaca', and a colon with direct speech and no guillemets. A reviewer should confirm the style.
Questions use rising intonation (Vous avez … ?, Il y a … ?, Il faut … ?). A reviewer should confirm this register over Est-ce que forms.
La serviette also means towel, and no disambiguating note is kept. Mexican Spanish mesero is rendered by the general French serveur.
The spaces before ? and : are ordinary spaces. A typographic no-break space policy is undecided.
